full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ: This appeal by leave is from an order dated 31st May 1992 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division rejecting Writ Petition No.1950 of 1992 filed by the appellant summarily. 

 15. It has been noticed above that respondent No.4 was entitled to get back the disputed land under the agreement if he had paid the consideration money back to the appellant within Agrahayan 1378 BS that is, within the next two years after the expiry of 5 years during which the appellant was to enjoy the usufruct of the disputed land. In the leave petition the appellant has stated that the right of reconveyance of respondent No.4 as per terms of the contemporaneous agreement expired on 10-1-1972 (the corresponding English date of the last day of Agrahayan 1378 BS will be 16-12-1971 and not 10.1.1972 as mentioned) long before the promulgation of President's Order No.88 of 1972. Admittedly respondent No.4 filed the redemption case on 25.6.1973 under President's Order No.88 of 1972 which came into force on 3-8-1972. The transaction between the parties undisputedly came to an end and became a past and closed transaction before 3-8-1972 when President's Order No.88 of 1972 became operative. It has been decided in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani. 32 DLR (AD) 233 that transactions which are past and closed before 3-8-1972 are not amenable to the operation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972. It is, therefore, clear that respondent No.4 could not claim redemption of the complete usufructuary mortgage as contemplated under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, briefly, the Act and the order passed in the redemption case on 15-6-1974 was therefore a void order. The only answer that Mr. Roushan Ali could advance in reply was that the provisions of section 95 of the Act were made applicable to all transfers as contemplated in section 95A of the Act "whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order 1972 "(President's Order No.88 of 1972). He wants to say that since President's Order No. 88 of 1972 was made operative retrospectively the transaction between the parties notwithstanding that the period thereunder expired before 3-8-1972 would attract the provisions of the said President's Order. This submission is wholly unacceptable because it fails to take into account "the doctrine of past and closed" as was indicated in the aforesaid case. Mr. Rowshan Ali argued that even without section 95A being there in the statute book the respondent could ask for redemption of the mortgage under sub-section (4) of section 95 of the Act or even under the ordinary law within a period of 60 years. So the relief obtained by the respondent cannot be said to be illegal or given without jurisdiction. This argument also is plainly untenable because the respondent sought relief specifically taking advantage of the provision of section 95A which was introduced by President's Order No. 88 of 1972 under which the transaction as between the parties in the present case was deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for the purpose of attraction of sub-sections (4) and (5) of section 95 of the Act. The contention of Mr. Roushan Ali pre-supposes that there was a transaction of mortgage between the parties even without the provision of section 95A of the Act. But that does not appear to have been the case of the respondent and that it could not have been so as a matter of fact because it was a case of an out and out sale with a contemporaneous agreement for reconveyance. Thus we find no difficulty in upholding the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the orders passed by respondent No.1 were clearly without jurisdiction.
